highlights: The thinking is that if frontier AI model makers can automate the development of their future models, it could create a feedback loop that could lead to a whirlwind pace of change in AI advancements. Chan cowrote a paper with Anthropic cofounder Jack Clark, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki, Microsoft chief scientific officer Eric Horvitz, and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton (among others) that urges policymakers to get insight into how top AI labs are automating their development, including some of the most cutting-edge research being done at companies like Anthropic and OpenAI. The process is often referred to as recursive self-improvement (RSI), but Chan said he prefers "intelligence explosion" because it allows for separate discussions of two themes: efforts to automate AI research and the question of whether automating research will lead to a skyrocketing improvement in AI capabilities. He said that an explosion could also lead to faster discoveries, including in areas like medicine.

highlights: # The 6G core divide. Three competing 6G core architectures threaten to splinter the global standard. * Direction 1 – Separate AI domain: A dedicated AI domain for intent handling independent of the packet-switched network, with the AMF routing NAS signaling while AI fulfillment occurs via SBI; backed by Nokia, T-Mobile USA, Verizon, NVIDIA, Deutsche Telekom, Apple\*, Qualcomm, Ericsson and NEC, though implementation requires complex UE AI domain client integration. Delegates are discussing a compromise: a partial merge of Directions 1 and 2 (AI functionality in 6G NFs), in which operators could separate the AI domain while introducing modular routing to prevent potential chokepoints in the AMF. By formalizing an intent-driven AI domain in the core network and device (Direction 1), 3GPP is fundamentally changing device architecture. It standardizes UE AI domain client interfaces to the core by creating an application-layer intent client to understand what the user or agent wants and a 3GPP AI domain client to translate that into secure network signaling.
